title: Exit codes and stderr conventions for CLIs
when: A CLI is used from scripts or CI and the user wants reliable exit statuses, clean stdout for data and readable error messages on stderr.
prompt:
Goal: A documented exit code table, one error path that maps error types to codes, data on stdout and every message on stderr.
Steps:
1. Table in README and code: 0 success, 1 runtime failure, 2 usage error, 3 partial success when a batch had failures, 130 interrupted by Ctrl+C. Alternatively use sysexits (64 usage, 65 bad data, 66 no input); pick one scheme.
2. class UsageError extends Error and class InputError extends Error; main() catches, maps the class to a code and prints "tool: message" to stderr.
3. Unexpected errors print one line plus "run with --debug for details"; --debug adds the stack.
4. Set process.exitCode and let the process end on its own so pending stdout flushes; call process.exit only after awaiting the last write.
5. process.on("SIGINT") stops the work, writes nothing more to stdout and sets 130.
6. --quiet hides info lines but never errors; --verbose adds detail on stderr only.
7. Warnings start with "warning:" on stderr and keep the exit code unless --strict.
Quality bar:
- tool > out.txt leaves only data in out.txt.
- Scripts can tell usage errors from runtime failures.
Pitfalls:
- console.log for errors, mixing them into piped data.
- process.exit(1) right after a large write, truncating output.
- Exit 0 when some items failed.
Verify:
- [ ] Exit code table documented.
- [ ] Errors use console.error or process.stderr.
- [ ] No process.exit before output is flushed.
- [ ] SIGINT gives 130.
Output: src/errors.mjs, the main wrapper in bin/tool.mjs and an Exit codes section in README.md.

examples.input: my script cannot tell if the tool failed, it always returns 0
examples.output: exit code table 0/1/2/3/130 in README, UsageError and InputError mapped in main, errors on stderr, --debug for stacks
